- .github/workflows/clarify.yml | severity=low | confidence=2
  Line or code reference: lines 447-451 (the `gh_retry_to_file` fallback body when `err_file` is empty after mktemp failure)
  PROBLEM: When `mktemp` fails and sets `err_file=""`, the else branch runs `"$@" > "${out}" && return 0`. On command failure (non-zero exit), the function falls through to retry logic without capturing stderr, so the permanent-failure grep detection (404, 422, "Resource not accessible") is lost. A definitive 4xx will consume the retry budget with backoff instead of returning immediately, and each retry will log the misleading "retrying in Xs" message as if a transient error occurred.
  WHY: `mktemp` failure on a GitHub Actions runner is extremely unlikely (`RUNNER_TEMP` is a built-in env var pointing to a writable directory), so this path is rarely exercised. When it does trigger, the only consequence is wasted retry budget on a permanent error — the function still reaches the max-attempts exit and the caller still falls through to the "final_merge_resume check failed" warning.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

- .github/workflows/clarify.yml | severity=low | confidence=2
  Line or code reference: lines 425-461 (the inline `gh_retry_to_file` fallback when `err_file` is empty after `mktemp` fails)
  PROBLEM: When `mktemp "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/gh_retry_fallback_stderr.XXXXXX"` fails and `err_file=""`, the fallback takes the `else` branch (`"$@" > "${out}" && return 0`) which runs the command without capturing stderr. The function then cannot grep for the `_is_gh_permanent_failure` patterns (404, 422, "resource not accessible") and falls through to the max-attempts path on every non-zero exit, including a definitive 404 or 422. The result is the retry budget being consumed (2+4+6+8 = 20s with the cap) and a misleading `::warning::gh_retry_to_file fallback: gh command failed (attempt N/M), retrying in Xs` message, even though the real helper would have stopped on the first attempt with the non-retryable warning.
  WHY: A degraded runner with no writable `RUNNER_TEMP` and a read-only `/tmp` (or any other `mktemp` failure path) silently disables the permanent-failure detection that this whole fallback was hardened to add. The conditions are narrow (`RUNNER_TEMP` invalid AND `/tmp` not writable AND the API call happens to return a 4xx) but the failure mode defeats the purpose of the new grep branch.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

The run still converges (the outer `::warning::final_merge_resume check failed` fires), but the degraded-mode optimization the rest of the fallback was built to provide is silently lost on the exact failure modes it was designed to detect.
